newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks halt record run on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks halt record run on profit-taking.

text.p: Mexican stocks fell for the first time in six sessions Thursday on profit-taking after the market's record-breaking run.
"The market just saw some profit-taking today, but is still firm," said Gerardo Copca, deputy research head at the Valores Finamex brokerage.
The blue-chip IPC share index lost 2.03 points on the day to 4,119.53.

Dealers said heavyweight Telmex stock also swayed the market, after closing down 10 centavos (1 cent) to 18.50 pesos ($2.32) in tandem with its ADRs, which bucked an upward trend on Wall Street to end off 5/8 at 46-1/4. The Dow Jones industrial average rose 35.63 to 7,305.29.
Trading volume was heavy at 141.5 million shares, although dealers said the total was misleading as cross trades accounted for more than 37 million shares.
On the broad market, 115 stocks changed hands, of which losers outnumbered gainers, 60-29.
Dealers said blue chips were notably absent from the big gainers' list, which was headed by infrequently traded stocks that had lagged behind the market.
Traders said the market could be influenced by U.S. market reaction on Friday to the U.S. May jobs report.
